intro: The long-horizon structural thesis is strengthening, not weakening, despite this week's FOMC hawkish shock. Three new data points since June 17 reinforce the long-term picture: (1) SK Hynix confirmed HBM4E sample shipments in H2 2026 — the HBM technology roadmap is accelerating faster than consensus; (2) the Iran ceasefire is in effect — the macro tailwind of Hormuz reopening removes the most persistent inflation overhang that has pressured the Fed; (3) NVDA held above $200 on below-average volume through the most hawkish FOMC since 2022 — institutional conviction in the AI capex thesis is demonstrated, not claimed. Warsh's 'no forward guidance' posture means the hawkish dots are aspirational, not committed — a single CPI print can reverse them. At the multi-quarter horizon, the AI supercycle, Starlink subscriber compounding, HBM4 constraint through 2028, and the post-Iran macro normalization are the durable drivers. Use FOMC-driven dislocations as accumulation opportunities.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: The toll road on AI compute — FOMC-driven pullbacks are accumulation windows, not thesis-enders.
ideas.why: NVDA's $25B bond sale ($85B orders, 3.4x oversubscribed) is management's public declaration of AI capex continuity regardless of the rate environment. The CUDA software moat, the Blackwell/Rubin roadmap, SK Hynix locked as primary memory supplier through 2030, Apple/Google PCC (Siri via Blackwell B200), and the $299 average analyst PT create a multi-year structural bid. The FOMC hawkish shock creates a near-term multiple headwind (higher discount rate on ~30x P/E), not a change in the trajectory of AI capex. The $195–$215 zone is the structural accumulation window — use it.
ideas.driver: Hyperscaler + sovereign AI capex compounding through 2028+; inference demand following training; HBM supply locked through multi-year partnerships; NVDA Annual Meeting June 24 as near-term catalyst.
ideas.risk: Custom ASICs (hyperscaler in-house silicon) eroding share faster than expected; or a Fed that actually delivers multiple hikes in 2026, creating a sustained 30Y above 5.00% that compresses the AI-capex multiple across the sector.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: HBM4E sampling confirmed for H2 2026 — the memory AI trade is entering its next product generation with the moat widening.
ideas.why: SK Hynix confirmed HBM4E sample shipments in H2 2026 (mass production 2027) — a positive surprise that was not in analyst models as of June 17. The HBM shortage running through 2028 (TradingKey), NVIDIA supply partnership through 2030, ~70% HBM market share, 72% Q1 operating margin, and a confirmed shareholder value enhancement review are all in place. The 38-analyst average PT of ₩2,690,000 has been exceeded — a PT revision cycle toward ₩3.0M–₩3.2M is now underway. The July 29 Q2 earnings call is the next catalyst to price HBM4E into the structural multiple. This is the highest-conviction long-term idea in the portfolio.
ideas.driver: HBM4→4E product transition with SK Hynix the clear technology leader; shortage extending through 2028; NVIDIA supply lock; sell-side PT revision cycle now underway as stock exceeds prior consensus.
ideas.risk: Samsung executes a credible HBM4 capacity ramp that takes market share; memory industry reverts to cyclical oversupply if AI capex cycle has a digestion pause.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: The lowest-risk path to enterprise AI monetization — the FOMC selloff to $378 is an accumulation opportunity.
ideas.why: Microsoft's enterprise AI thesis is compounding: Azure AI workloads are inflecting, Copilot attach rates across hundreds of millions of enterprise seats are growing, and the OpenAI investment provides asymmetric exposure to frontier model development. At ~$378, the post-FOMC selloff offers a better entry than any time since SPCX briefly overtook MSFT's market cap (a thin-float artifact). The recurring-revenue model makes Microsoft structurally less sensitive to rate-hike uncertainty than pure-growth names — cash flows are real, current, and compounding. The $375–$390 zone is the structural accumulation window.
ideas.driver: Azure AI workload attach rates + Copilot enterprise adoption across installed base of hundreds of millions of seats; OpenAI relationship providing frontier model access.
ideas.risk: AI capex-to-monetization ratio deteriorates (spending accelerating faster than revenue); antitrust scrutiny of the OpenAI relationship; SPCX and new-AI-infrastructure narrative pulling growth capital allocation away from 'old AI' incumbents.

ideas.name: Alphabet
ideas.idea: The cheapest AI full-stack at the megacap cohort's lowest multiple — search cannibalization risk is priced too harshly.
ideas.why: Alphabet owns Gemini (frontier models), TPUs (cost-competitive inference), Google Cloud (inflecting), and search (generating the cash to fund all of it). The market prices a high probability of secular search decline that is not yet appearing in revenue data. At ~$355 post-FOMC selloff, the forward multiple is the cheapest in the megacap cohort. If AI Overviews prove to be a moat-extender (users stay on Google longer and see more premium ads), the re-rating is a multi-year compounding opportunity. Iran oil disinflation → lower DXY medium-term is a structural tailwind for Alphabet's emerging-market ad revenue.
ideas.driver: TPU-driven inference cost advantage; Gemini integration across a billion-user surface; Google Cloud AI workloads inflecting; potential search moat expansion rather than cannibalization.
ideas.risk: Genuine query erosion to AI assistants at scale (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) compounds advertising revenue decline; antitrust remedies fracturing the search + advertising bundle; higher-for-longer rates extend the multiple compression.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: A generational franchise — use the entry-zone window to build a put-hedged position before the MSCI passive bid exhausts.
ideas.why: SpaceX owns the only proven reusable orbital launch system at scale, Starlink at 5M+ subscribers growing ~40% annually, Starshield national-security contracts, and now an AI coding platform via the Cursor/Anysphere acquisition ($60B stock). The MSCI passive bid creates a 2–4 week float-squeeze window where price is temporarily disconnected from fundamentals. The structural trade: enter the $190–$200 zone with a put hedge (eliminating the downside tail) and hold for the 3–5 year franchise compounding story. The December 2026 lock-up expiry is the first major supply event — before that, float mechanics keep the support bid strong.
ideas.driver: Starlink subscriber and ARPU compounding toward a recurring-revenue connectivity utility; Starship reducing cost-to-orbit toward near-zero; Cursor AI software layer adding recurring software revenue to the infrastructure franchise.
ideas.risk: IPO-cycle overvaluation creates a poor structural entry if the passive bid exhausts before fundamentals support the $190+ price level; key-person concentration; first earnings print (September 2) reveals the true revenue structure and may disappoint vs. the $2T+ market cap expectation.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: Hold through the post-FOMC stop-risk window — the structural adoption thesis is intact; the IBIT outflow is a cyclical disruption, not a structural reversal.
ideas.why: The June 2026 FOMC hawkish shock (rate hike odds ~80%, DXY above 100) is a cyclical headwind against the structural BTC adoption thesis. The thesis: fixed supply + ETF access (IBIT, FBTC, BITA) + corporate treasury ownership (Strategy) + halving cycle supply reduction + Warsh's 'no forward guidance' = inherently more reactive Fed policy + Iran ceasefire → oil lower → CPI relief → DXY peaks. The IBIT outflow ($31M June 17) is notable but not structural: it's one session in a product with $60B+ AUM. LTH accumulation of 125,000 BTC in June is the counter-signal that the smart money is not abandoning the thesis. At the multi-year horizon, the primary driver remains the halving cycle and the widening institutional access ramp.
ideas.driver: Fixed supply meeting widening institutional access (ETFs, corporate treasuries) across halving cycles; DXY structural decline medium-term as Hormuz reopening removes the oil-inflation driver; monetary policy uncertainty favoring hard assets.
ideas.risk: A committed hawkish Fed cycle (Warsh actually delivers multiple hikes, not just aspirational dots) creates a multi-quarter DXY strength regime that is structurally bearish for BTC; IBIT outflows that accelerate to $100M+/day for 5+ sessions would signal institutional exit, not cyclical rotation.

ideas.name: Amazon
ideas.idea: AWS AI is the cloud-infra winner that post-FOMC selloff makes more attractive at $183.
ideas.why: Amazon runs the world's largest commercial cloud (AWS), is ramping custom silicon (Trainium, Inferentia) to reduce AI inference costs for its own and third-party workloads, and has a logistics network that scales into robotic AI. The FOMC-driven selloff of -3.46% on June 17 brings AMZN to ~$183 — the most attractive valuation in the megacap cloud cohort. AWS AI workloads are inflecting; Prime and logistics economics are compounding. The SPCX/NVDA narrative has temporarily obscured AMZN's AI story, creating an entry opportunity for investors who can look past the IPO headline cycle.
ideas.driver: AWS AI workload attach rates + Trainium/Inferentia inference cost advantage; Prime and logistics flywheel compounding at scale; Hormuz reopening reducing shipping cost inflation.
ideas.risk: Cloud spending deceleration if enterprise IT budgets tighten in a higher-rate environment; competitive pressure from Azure and Google Cloud on AI workload share; custom silicon ramp extends timelines.
